cells.tense: Right now you are inside the satisfaction and can let it set the pace of what moves next.
cells.act: move at the pace your feeling can sustain
cells.ask: Take the next piece of work at the speed your feeling can carry without fraying. Steady, no surging. When you catch yourself pushing past that, ease back — that easing is the whole practice.
cells.core:
Something false has come down quickly and what is left standing is lighter than you expected. The satisfaction you have in what you imagined is the real kind — not because things are perfect but because you have felt them through. That is available now, and the pull is to pour it straight into the next move at top speed.

What is called for here is not more drive. It is letting the push and the pull go the same direction and finding the pace you can keep. Take the next piece of work at the speed your feeling can carry without fraying. Steady, not surging. When you catch yourself pushing past that, ease back — that easing is the whole practice. The clearing already happened; keeping it clear is the work now.
cells.sheetLine: The clearing is done — move at the pace your feeling can hold.
cells.verb: having imagined at length and finding the satisfaction in it
cells.place: a sudden clearing, once the false structure goes

cells.tense: You are already tending outcomes that have not yet happened, and the tending is outrunning what is actually growing.
cells.act: look after what grows with a steady hand
cells.ask: Tend what you are currently forcing with a steady hand: water it, look after it, add nothing more. Watch for the pull to add and set the matter down where it stands.
cells.core:
A structure has come down fast and you are standing in the open part of it, and the energy that was holding the old thing up has nowhere to go but forward. So you are already shaping what is next before it has had a chance to happen — deciding how it turns out, protecting it from a failure it has not met yet. It reads as care. The people getting tended can feel the difference between that and room.

What fits here is tending, not more effort. Look after what you are currently forcing with a steady hand — water it, add nothing more than that. Tend without clutching. The clearing already happened; you do not have to keep building over it. Watch for the pull to add, and set the matter down where it stands.

cells.tense: You are still at the threshold of something that already ended, weighing a call the clearing has already made.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: Hold only your own take on what the clearing settled — quiet, no deciding, no announcing — for a week. If a choice pushes, note the push and leave the page open.
cells.core:
The falseness came down around you and you are still going over it from where the old structure was. There is a call to make and you are holding the two sides of it side by side, not committing, not moving, so the aliveness is elsewhere and you are at the threshold of a place you already left. That is what not-arriving looks like from here — not resistance, just a hand still on the door.

What charges this is reflective knowing. Hold only your own take on what the clearing settled — quiet, no deciding, no announcing — for a week. If a choice pushes at you, note it and leave the page open. Weighing is not the same as waiting, and nothing has to be declared yet.

cells.tense: You are doing the sorting and refining right now, and you speak about it as if it were happening to you.
cells.act: refine one distinction by close attention
cells.ask: Refine a distinction you keep letting blur — is this mine or theirs, is this settled or not — by close attention for two minutes, then say which it is. That call was yours.
cells.core:
The clearing is in your hands — you are the one letting the false structure fall and refining what stays — and your account of it has you reading the wind. It is not reading; it is discernment, practised, and it is going well. Practice has been doing something through you and the label you have put on it is temperament.

Go back to the earlier form of it: the smaller practice before it became a way of living. Refine a distinction you keep letting blur — is this mine or theirs, is this settled or not — by close attention for two minutes, then say which it is. That call was yours. Refinement serves the growth, not a worry. Say what you did.
